content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I have a damper actuator with a 500 ohm input impedance for 0-20mA signals. I also have an [product_name] analog output module. According to the catalog, the resistance between the M and I ports should be less than 250 ohms. What will happen if I connect the actuator to this analog output module? I've already purchased this equipment and can't replace it. I need to use what I have. Any advice would be appreciated.

analysis.insight_summary: The user is worried about whether it's safe to use an [product_name] analog output module with a damper actuator that has a higher input impedance than recommended in the documentation from [company_name]. The main concern is about possible problems or risks when operating equipment outside specified compatibility limits, especially regarding output impedance.
analysis.user_expectations: The user hopes that the [product_name] analog output module will work reliably with a device that has a load impedance above the recommended value. They are looking for confirmation or guidance on if the setup will function correctly, or what issues to expect.
